text: Every team has had this moment: wait, didn't we already decide not to do that? Precedent is a decision memory that acts. It catches the contradiction in Confluence, in Jira, in your workflow, and in your AI coding agent.

It starts where teams already write. In this architecture review, the payments team decided, with a slash decision, to keep all transactional payment data in PostgreSQL. Precedent captures it with its owner, date and rationale, and the page shows which Jira work contradicts it.

Months later, someone files new work: move payout reconciliation to MongoDB. Before they even press create, Jira's own create dialog warns them: already decided in D E C one, with who decided, when, and what to use instead.

If it is filed anyway, the Precedent panel flags the conflict, quotes the sentence that tripped the guardrail, and offers a one click compliant alternative. Precedent also keeps a short brief for coding agents in the work item: what to do, which packages are denied, and which code the decision governs.
And it is enforced in the workflow. Moving the work item to Done is blocked while the conflict is unresolved, unless the team reviews it or logs an exception.

Ask Precedent hands the work item to the Rovo agent. It explains why the decision was made, who owns it, and the options: comply, log an exception, or supersede the decision, citing the source every time.
Now a developer opens the work item in Claude Code, straight from Jira. Jira hands over the summary and the description, and with it, the Precedent brief.

This is a real Claude Code session with exactly that prompt. Before writing a line of code, the agent stops: the task would break D E C one. It reads the ledger code, explains why the decision exists, and proposes a PostgreSQL JSON B design instead, or an exception for the owner to approve.

Decisions stay alive. Tripwires watch the assumptions behind them: when shared Redis incidents pile up, the Radar turns red and the owner is asked to review. Meeting notes feed a decision inbox, and Rovo Search finds every decision through the Teamwork Graph.
Precedent. One Forge app that runs entirely on Atlassian, so your team, and your agents, know what has already been decided.
